MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the

contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

}


PUBLIC COMMENTS PERTAINING TO STUDY SESSION / CLOSED SESSION ITEMS (3 Minute Time Limit) {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Debra Falese, a resident of Huntington Beach, was called to speak and stated her opinion that Huntington Beach can successfully address the issue of airplane noise in order to maintain property values and quality of life.\par
\par
Mario Taberniy, a 45 year resident of Huntington Beach, was called to speak and stated his opinion that the Air Traffic Noise Working Group should be a permanent, on-going commission, to address the nuisance and health issues related to local air traffic.\par
\par
Lou Penrose, former District Chief of Staff for U.S. Congressman John Campbell, was called to speak and congratulated Council members Brenden and Delgleize for their focus and efforts on this very complicated issue.\par
\par
Laurel Armor, a resident since 1973, was called to speak and shared her opinion that the issues related to air traffic have only been getting worse.\par
\par
John Anderson, a resident on Bolsa Chica since 2010, was called to speak and voiced his opinion that the noise level from aircraft has definitely increased over the years, and he believes there are acceptable adjustments that can be made to reduce the local impact.\par
}


STUDY SESSION

2.. Air Traffic Noise Update {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Councilmember Brenden introduced Phil Burtis, member of the Air Traffic Noise Working Group (ATNWG) who presented a PowerPoint communication entitled Air Traffic Noise Working Group Final Report with slides titled: Background, Key Objectives, Objectives: All Met, Members, Member Profiles, Current Noise Complaints from LAX, Current Noise Complaints from LGB, The Recommendation, Jet Noise Commission (2), How Did We Get to This Recommendation?, ATNWG Action Plan, Identify the Issues, The Consensus on Issues, Investigation, The Change by the FAA, NextGen Resulted In:, LGB Arrivals: Aug 2016, LGB Arrivals: Aug 2017, Pathways to Remediation (2), The Environmental Assessment, Pathways to Remediation, Legislative Actions, Pathways to Remediation, Collaborative Actions, and Summary.\par
\par
Councilmember Semeta and Mr. Burtis discussed some of the FAA plane route procedure changes which unfortunately produced increased noise for homes under flight paths and at the present it is unknown when and how the FAA may plan further modifications.  Councilmember Semeta asked for more details regarding the recommendation to change from a Working Group to a Commission.\par
\par
Councilmembers Brenden and Delgleize explained that a Commission is more appropriate than an Ad Hoc Committee for an issue that is not going to go away and is expected to require long-term diligence.\par
\par
Councilmember O'Connell stated his support for a Commission and continued collaboration to produce solutions that mitigate the negative impacts to residents.  Councilmember O'Connell expressed his appreciation for the outstanding work and progress of the Ad Hoc Committee.\par
\par
Councilmember Hardy expressed her appreciation for the Working Group presentation which helped her understand the need for a Commission.\par
\par
Mayor Posey expressed his appreciation to the Ad Hoc Working Group members for their dedication to staying on top of the issue.\par
\par
Councilmember Brenden explained that this Study Session presentation was to bring everyone up to date on the topic, and at the next Council meeting there will be an action item addressing the Ad Hoc Working Group's recommendations.  Councilmember Brenden also expressed his appreciation and gratitude to several Ad Hoc Working Group members such as Scott Combest, Chris Kunze, Michael Bourgeault and Mario Tabernig.\par
}


1.. Presentation of potential modifications in the Huntington Beach Tourism Business Improvement District (TBID) - Visit Huntington Beach {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Wilson introduced Kelly Miller, President and CEO of Visit Huntington Beach (VHB), Justin Simpson, Chair of VHB, General Manager of the Shorebreak Kimpton Hotel and Gina Trechter of Civitas, who jointly presented a PowerPoint communication entitled HBTBID Study Session with the following slides titled: History of Huntington Beach TBID, Two Current Agreements: City of Huntington Beach & Visit Huntington Beach, HBTBID Assessment Modification (4), Gina Trechter - Civitas, Tourism District Stats, Tourism Improvement Districts as of September 14, 2017, Renewal Process/Timeline, TOT and TBID Rates/Total Check Out Rates, and Thank You!\par
\par
Councilmember Delgleize and presenters discussed how the amount of assessment change was determined, and the agreement term of 7.5 years.\par
\par
Councilmember Brenden and presenters discussed how the 7.5 year term was reached, and some specifics related to distribution of Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) funds and budget categories.\par
\par
Councilmember Semeta echoed the comments of appreciation made by Councilmembers Delgleize and Brenden for the efforts put forth by Visit Huntington Beach regarding enhancing income in a reasonable way that will not negatively impact the tourist industry.\par
\par
Councilmember Hardy confirmed that TBID is not getting more money from the proposed changes, but the increase comes to the City.\par
\par
Councilmember O'Connell and presenters discussed that TOT income has increased and appears to be holding steady.  The recent hotel enhancements and added restaurants are expected to keep that 5 - 10% growth trend going.\par
\par
Mayor Posey discussed with the presenters that future efforts will be addressing ways to increase visits outside of the peak summer season.\par
}
